final_proof:
Let \(K\) be a subfield of \(\mathbb C\). Recall that the characteristic of a field \(F\) is the least positive integer \(n\), if one exists, for which
\[
n1_F=\underbrace{1_F+\cdots+1_F}_{n\text{ summands}}=0_F;
\]
if no such positive integer exists, then \(\operatorname{char}(F)=0\).

First, \(1_K=1_{\mathbb C}\). Indeed, choose any nonzero \(a\in K\), which is possible because a field is nontrivial. Since multiplication on \(K\) is the restriction of multiplication on \(\mathbb C\), the equality \(1_Ka=a\) holds in \(\mathbb C\). Multiplying by \(a^{-1}\) in \(\mathbb C\) gives \(1_K=1_{\mathbb C}\). Likewise, the additive identity of \(K\) is \(0_{\mathbb C}\).

Now let \(n\) be any positive integer. Addition in \(K\) is inherited from \(\mathbb C\), so
\[
n1_K=n1_{\mathbb C}.
\]
The right-hand side is the complex number whose real part is the positive integer \(n\), and therefore it is not \(0_{\mathbb C}\). Thus \(n1_K\ne 0_K\) for every positive integer \(n\). By the definition of characteristic, \(\operatorname{char}(K)=0\).
